issues.legal_issue: Failure to provide the accused with prosecution documents before a sessions inquiry does not automatically invalidate the commitment proceedings or trial when the failure caused no prejudice to the defence.
material_facts: The police officer failed to provide the accused with copies of the prosecution documents, and the committing magistrate failed to ensure that the copies were furnished during the inquiry.
The accused did not raise the omission before the committing magistrate or the Sessions Court; the issue was first raised in the appeals to the High Court.

The accused received the necessary copies in the Sessions Court before prosecution witnesses were examined there, and did not show that the time available prevented effective cross-examination or that an adjournment was needed.
The evidence against the accused was accepted by the courts below, and the conviction was unassailable on its merits.
No prejudice to the accused’s defence was shown.
issues.conclusion: The omissions were non-prejudicial irregularities, not defects that invalidated the commitment proceedings or trial, and were cured under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The word “shall” in sections 173(4) and 207A(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is directory, not mandatory. The magistrate must ensure that the accused receives the necessary documents, and must be alert to any resulting handicap to the defence. If non-compliance causes prejudice, the court may reopen the proceedings and require full compliance; if it causes no prejudice, it is an irregularity curable under section 537. The Court applied Abdul Rahman v. The King-Emperor, (1929) L.R. 55 I.A. 96, and Pulukuri Kotayya v. King-Emperor, (1947) L.R. 74 I.A. 65, and noted its similar approach in Gurbachan Singh v. The State of Punjab, Criminal Appeal No. 48 of 1957.

rule.if: sessions_trial_on_police_report and (police_failed_to_supply_copies or magistrate_failed_to_ensure_copies) and not defence_prejudice_shown

predicates.sessions_trial_on_police_report: The accused was committed for trial in the court of session following an inquiry on a police report.
predicates.police_failed_to_supply_copies: The investigating police officer did not furnish the accused with the prosecution documents intended to be relied on.
predicates.magistrate_failed_to_ensure_copies: The magistrate conducting the inquiry did not ensure that the accused received the prosecution documents.
predicates.defence_prejudice_shown: The accused showed that the failure to provide the documents handicapped the defence.
predicates.proceedings_not_vitiated: The commitment proceedings and trial remain valid despite the failure to provide the documents.

issues.definition: When a sessions trial follows a police report, failure by the police to supply prosecution documents or by the magistrate to ensure their supply does not invalidate the proceedings if the accused has not shown resulting prejudice to the defence.
